$comment: Advisories consciously accepted, read by scripts/audit-ci.mjs.
Every entry MUST carry an expiry date. A permanent exception is how a known
vulnerability becomes permanent; an expiring one forces the decision to be
made again once a fix may exist. An expired entry stops suppressing and the
build goes red, which is the intended behaviour, not a bug.
'reason' must say why the advisory is not reachable HERE — not that it is
inconvenient to fix. If the honest reason is 'no time', that is a risk
acceptance and belongs in the risk register, not in a build config.
One entry, added 2026-11-10: zod 3 memory advisory, pending the zod 4 upgrade.
It expires on 2026-12-10; the build goes red again then unless zod 4 is in.

allow.reason: Impact is bounded here, not absent. The advisory is memory growth while zod validates oversized collections that carry size constraints. Every request body passes express.json and urlencoded with a 1 MB limit (artifacts/api-server/src/app.ts) and requestGuard, which refuses bodies with more than 20,000 keys, arrays longer than 20,000 items or nesting deeper than 20 (artifacts/api-server/src/middleware/requestGuard.ts) before any zod schema runs, so the input an attacker controls is capped. The fix exists only in zod 4 (>=4.6.6), a major upgrade that also changes the generated schemas (orval.config.ts pins zod 3 output) and drizzle-zod; it is scheduled before this entry expires.
